<summary>Turned the Sales Ops request into one user story with 7 testable acceptance criteria: onboarding Case creation, Account activation, amount-based priority, de-duplication per Account, firing only on the transition to Closed Won, 200-record bulk safety, and least-privilege access for Standard User reps via a permission set. Identified two new fields (Account.Customer_Status__c, Case.Is_Onboarding__c) and assumed the standard "Closed Won" stage and Case object are in use.</summary>
<file path="docs/requirements.md">
# Closed Won → onboarding handoff (Sales Cloud)

## User story
**As a** Sales Operations manager
**I want** an onboarding Case to be created automatically when an Opportunity is Closed Won
**So that** the onboarding team starts immediately and no customer is missed.

## Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion |
|----|-----------|
| AC-1 | When an Opportunity becomes Closed Won, one Case is created on its Account with Subject "Onboarding: <Account Name>", Origin "Sales Handoff" and the onboarding flag set. |
| AC-2 | The Account's Customer Status is set to "Active Customer". |
| AC-3 | Case Priority is High when Opportunity Amount >= 100,000, otherwise Medium (blank amount = 0). |
| AC-4 | No new onboarding Case if the Account already has an open one; one Case per Account even when several of its Opportunities close in the same transaction (highest amount decides priority). |
| AC-5 | Fires only on the transition into Closed Won (insert as won, or update from a non-won stage). Later edits and Closed Lost do nothing. |
| AC-6 | Works for Data Loader batches of 200 Opportunities without hitting governor limits. |
| AC-7 | A Standard User sales rep with the "Onboarding Automation" permission set can close a deal and the automation succeeds; no profile changes. |

## Impacted objects and fields
| Object | Field | Type | New? |
|--------|-------|------|------|
| Account | Customer_Status__c | Picklist (Prospect, Active Customer, Former Customer) | New |
| Case | Is_Onboarding__c | Checkbox | New |
| Opportunity | StageName, IsWon, Amount, AccountId | Standard | Existing |

## Personas and access
- Sales rep (Standard User profile): closes Opportunities; needs Case create and edit access to Customer Status, granted by permission set.
- Onboarding team: works the Cases (existing access, out of scope).

## Volumes
- Up to 200 Opportunities per Data Loader batch; Opportunity updates throughout the day.

## Assumptions
- Standard "Closed Won" stage (IsWon = true). Multi-currency not enabled; Amount is in the corporate currency.
- Case assignment rules / queues are handled by existing org configuration.

## Out of scope
- Case assignment to a specific queue, email notifications, reopening onboarding for returning customers.
</file>

<summary>Chose an Apex trigger with a handler and a bulk-safe service over a record-triggered Flow, because AC-4 (one case per Account across a batch, highest amount wins) and AC-6 (200-record loads with an explicit SOQL budget) are simpler to guarantee and test in Apex. Designed two new fields, a least-privilege permission set, a logic-free trigger, OpportunityTriggerHandler and OnboardingService with one SOQL and two DML per transaction in user mode, and the OnboardingServiceTest class, with every acceptance criterion mapped.</summary>
<file path="docs/design.md">
# Solution design: Closed Won → onboarding handoff

## Clicks vs code
| Option | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| Record-triggered Flow | Meets AC-1/2/3/5, but AC-4 (one Case per Account across a 200-record batch, highest amount wins) needs collection logic that is hard to read and test in Flow. |
| **Apex trigger + service (chosen)** | Explicit bulk de-duplication, a fixed SOQL/DML budget, and unit tests per acceptance criterion. |

## Data model
- `Account.Customer_Status__c` – restricted picklist: Prospect, Active Customer, Former Customer; history tracked.
- `Case.Is_Onboarding__c` – checkbox, default false; identifies onboarding Cases (no subject matching).

## Automation
```
OpportunityTrigger (after insert, after update)        // no logic, one trigger per object
  -> OpportunityTriggerHandler.run()                   // routes by Trigger context
       -> OnboardingService.handleClosedWon(List<Opportunity> newOpps, Map<Id, Opportunity> oldMap)
```
`handleClosedWon` algorithm (bulk-safe):
1. Collect Opportunities that just became won (`IsWon` and old not won, or insert) with an AccountId;
   keep one per Account, the highest Amount (blank = 0).
2. ONE query: Accounts in that set with a subquery of open onboarding Cases (`LIMIT 1`), `WITH USER_MODE`.
3. Build Account updates (Customer_Status__c = Active Customer) and Cases for Accounts with no open onboarding Case.
4. TWO DML statements: `insert as user` Cases, `update as user` Accounts.
Constants: Origin "Sales Handoff", status "Active Customer", high-priority threshold 100,000.

## Security
- All classes `with sharing`; SOQL `WITH USER_MODE`; DML `as user`.
- Permission set `Onboarding_Automation`: Case read/create, edit on `Account.Customer_Status__c` and `Case.Is_Onboarding__c`,
  Apex class access. No profile changes.

## Files
| Owner | File |
|-------|------|
| Developer | objects/Account/fields/Customer_Status__c.field-meta.xml |
| Developer | objects/Case/fields/Is_Onboarding__c.field-meta.xml |
| Developer | permissionsets/Onboarding_Automation.permissionset-meta.xml |
| Developer | triggers/OpportunityTrigger.trigger (+ meta) |
| Developer | classes/OpportunityTriggerHandler.cls, classes/OnboardingService.cls (+ meta) |
| Test | classes/OnboardingServiceTest.cls (+ meta) |

## Governor-limit budget
1 SOQL + 2 DML per trigger invocation, independent of batch size (200 records → still 1 SOQL).

## Traceability
| AC | Design element |
|----|----------------|
| AC-1 | step 3 case build, Is_Onboarding__c |
| AC-2 | step 3 account update |
| AC-3 | threshold constant, highest amount per Account |
| AC-4 | step 1 one-per-Account, step 2 open-case subquery |
| AC-5 | step 1 transition check |
| AC-6 | single query + two DML |
| AC-7 | permission set, user-mode operations |
</file>

/**
 * Routes Opportunity trigger events to services. Keeps the trigger itself logic-free.
 */
public with sharing class OpportunityTriggerHandler {
    /** Entry point called from OpportunityTrigger. */
    public static void run() {
        if (Trigger.isAfter && Trigger.isInsert) {
            OnboardingService.handleClosedWon((List<Opportunity>) Trigger.new, null);
        } else if (Trigger.isAfter && Trigger.isUpdate) {
            OnboardingService.handleClosedWon(
                (List<Opportunity>) Trigger.new,
                (Map<Id, Opportunity>) Trigger.oldMap
            );
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Creates onboarding Cases and activates Accounts when Opportunities become Closed Won.
 */
public with sharing class OnboardingService {
    @TestVisible
    private static final String CASE_ORIGIN = 'Sales Handoff';
    @TestVisible
    private static final String ACTIVE_STATUS = 'Active Customer';
    @TestVisible
    private static final Decimal HIGH_PRIORITY_AMOUNT = 100000;

    /**
     * @param newOpps Trigger.new
     * @param oldMap  Trigger.oldMap (null on insert)
     */
    public static void handleClosedWon(List<Opportunity> newOpps, Map<Id, Opportunity> oldMap) {
        for (Opportunity opp : newOpps) {
            Opportunity old = oldMap == null ? null : oldMap.get(opp.Id);
            Boolean becameWon = opp.IsWon && (old == null || !old.IsWon);
            if (!becameWon || opp.AccountId == null) {
                continue;
            }

            Account acc = [
                SELECT Id, Name,
                    (SELECT Id FROM Cases WHERE Is_Onboarding__c = true AND IsClosed = false LIMIT 1)
                FROM Account
                WHERE Id = :opp.AccountId
                WITH USER_MODE
            ];
            if (acc.Cases.isEmpty()) {
                Decimal amount = opp.Amount == null ? 0 : opp.Amount;
                insert as user new Case(
                    AccountId = acc.Id,
                    Subject = 'Onboarding: ' + acc.Name,
                    Origin = CASE_ORIGIN,
                    Priority = amount >= HIGH_PRIORITY_AMOUNT ? 'High' : 'Medium',
                    Is_Onboarding__c = true,
                    Description = 'Created automatically from Closed Won opportunity ' + opp.Name
                );
            }
            update as user new Account(Id = acc.Id, Customer_Status__c = ACTIVE_STATUS);
        }
    }
}

<summary>Wrote OnboardingServiceTest with 9 test methods derived from the acceptance criteria and design only: case creation, account activation, priority boundary (100,000 vs 99,999.99), duplicate prevention, one case per Account per batch, transition-only firing, Closed Lost, a 200-Opportunity bulk load that also asserts the SOQL budget, and a System.runAs Standard User with the permission set.</summary>
<file path="force-app/main/default/classes/OnboardingServiceTest.cls">
/**
 * Tests derived from docs/requirements.md (AC-1 .. AC-7).
 */
@IsTest
private class OnboardingServiceTest {
    private static final String WON = 'Closed Won';
    private static final String OPEN_STAGE = 'Prospecting';

    @TestSetup
    static void setup() {
        insert new Account(Name = 'Acme Corp');
    }

    private static Account acme() {
        return [SELECT Id, Name, Customer_Status__c FROM Account WHERE Name = 'Acme Corp' LIMIT 1];
    }

    private static Opportunity newOpp(Id accountId, String stage, Decimal amount) {
        return new Opportunity(
            Name = 'Deal ' + amount, AccountId = accountId, StageName = stage,
            CloseDate = Date.today(), Amount = amount
        );
    }

    private static List<Case> onboardingCases(Id accountId) {
        return [SELECT Id, Subject, Origin, Priority FROM Case WHERE AccountId = :accountId AND Is_Onboarding__c = true];
    }

    @IsTest
    static void closedWonCreatesOnboardingCase() {
        Account acc = acme();
        Opportunity opp = newOpp(acc.Id, OPEN_STAGE, 5000);
        insert opp;

        Test.startTest();
        opp.StageName = WON;
        update opp;
        Test.stopTest();

        List<Case> cases = onboardingCases(acc.Id);
        Assert.areEqual(1, cases.size(), 'AC-1: exactly one onboarding case expected');
        Assert.areEqual('Onboarding: Acme Corp', cases[0].Subject, 'AC-1: subject format');
        Assert.areEqual('Sales Handoff', cases[0].Origin, 'AC-1: origin');
    }

    @IsTest
    static void closedWonActivatesAccount() {
        Account acc = acme();
        Test.startTest();
        insert newOpp(acc.Id, WON, 5000);
        Test.stopTest();

        Assert.areEqual('Active Customer', acme().Customer_Status__c, 'AC-2: account must be activated');
    }

    @IsTest
    static void priorityDependsOnAmount() {
        Account other = new Account(Name = 'Globex');
        insert other;
        Test.startTest();
        insert new List<Opportunity>{ newOpp(acme().Id, WON, 100000), newOpp(other.Id, WON, 99999.99) };
        Test.stopTest();

        Assert.areEqual('High', onboardingCases(acme().Id)[0].Priority, 'AC-3: >= 100,000 is High');
        Assert.areEqual('Medium', onboardingCases(other.Id)[0].Priority, 'AC-3: below 100,000 is Medium');
    }

    @IsTest
    static void noDuplicateWhenOpenOnboardingCaseExists() {
        Account acc = acme();
        insert new Case(AccountId = acc.Id, Subject = 'Existing', Is_Onboarding__c = true, Status = 'New');

        Test.startTest();
        insert newOpp(acc.Id, WON, 5000);
        Test.stopTest();

        Assert.areEqual(1, onboardingCases(acc.Id).size(), 'AC-4: no duplicate onboarding case');
    }

    @IsTest
    static void multipleWonOpportunitiesForSameAccountCreateOneCase() {
        Account acc = acme();
        Test.startTest();
        insert new List<Opportunity>{ newOpp(acc.Id, WON, 1000), newOpp(acc.Id, WON, 250000) };
        Test.stopTest();

        List<Case> cases = onboardingCases(acc.Id);
        Assert.areEqual(1, cases.size(), 'AC-4: one case per account per batch');
        Assert.areEqual('High', cases[0].Priority, 'AC-3/AC-4: highest amount decides priority');
    }

    @IsTest
    static void onlyFiresOnTransitionToClosedWon() {
        Account acc = acme();
        Opportunity opp = newOpp(acc.Id, WON, 5000);
        insert opp;
        delete onboardingCases(acc.Id);

        Test.startTest();
        opp.Description = 'Edited after closing';
        update opp;
        Test.stopTest();

        Assert.areEqual(0, onboardingCases(acc.Id).size(), 'AC-5: editing a won opportunity must not re-fire');
    }

    @IsTest
    static void nonWonStageDoesNothing() {
        Account acc = acme();
        Test.startTest();
        insert newOpp(acc.Id, 'Closed Lost', 5000);
        Test.stopTest();

        Assert.areEqual(0, onboardingCases(acc.Id).size(), 'AC-5: lost deals create no case');
        Assert.isNull(acme().Customer_Status__c, 'AC-5: lost deals do not activate the account');
    }

    @IsTest
    static void bulkLoadOf200OpportunitiesStaysWithinLimits() {
        List<Account> accounts = new List<Account>();
        for (Integer i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
            accounts.add(new Account(Name = 'Bulk ' + i));
        }
        insert accounts;
        List<Opportunity> opps = new List<Opportunity>();
        for (Account a : accounts) {
            opps.add(newOpp(a.Id, WON, 1000));
        }

        Test.startTest();
        insert opps;
        Integer queries = Limits.getQueries();
        Test.stopTest();

        Assert.areEqual(200, [SELECT COUNT() FROM Case WHERE Is_Onboarding__c = true AND Account.Name LIKE 'Bulk %'],
            'AC-6: one case per account in a 200-record load');
        Assert.isTrue(queries <= 5, 'AC-6: SOQL usage must not grow with batch size, used ' + queries);
    }

    @IsTest
    static void salesUserWithPermissionSetCanCloseDeal() {
        Profile standard = [SELECT Id FROM Profile WHERE Name = 'Standard User' LIMIT 1];
        User rep = new User(
            Alias = 'srep', Email = 'sales.rep@example.com', EmailEncodingKey = 'UTF-8', LastName = 'Rep',
            LanguageLocaleKey = 'en_US', LocaleSidKey = 'en_US', ProfileId = standard.Id,
            TimeZoneSidKey = 'Asia/Kolkata', Username = 'sales.rep.' + System.now().getTime() + '@example.com'
        );
        insert rep;
        PermissionSet ps = [SELECT Id FROM PermissionSet WHERE Name = 'Onboarding_Automation' LIMIT 1];
        insert new PermissionSetAssignment(AssigneeId = rep.Id, PermissionSetId = ps.Id);

        System.runAs(rep) {
            Account acc = new Account(Name = 'Rep Account');
            insert acc;
            Test.startTest();
            insert newOpp(acc.Id, WON, 5000);
            Test.stopTest();
            Assert.areEqual(1, onboardingCases(acc.Id).size(), 'AC-7: permission set grants what the automation needs');
        }
    }
}

<summary>Fixed the static-analysis findings: OnboardingService ran a SOQL query and two DML statements inside the per-Opportunity loop (OperationWithLimitsInLoop x3), which would exceed governor limits on a 200-record Data Loader batch (200 queries vs the 100 limit), and it took the case priority from whichever deal was processed first instead of the highest amount (AC-4). Rewrote it to the designed bulk pattern: collect one won Opportunity per Account, one Account query with an open-onboarding-case subquery, then one insert and one update. Split helpers to bring cognitive complexity under the threshold.</summary>
<file path="force-app/main/default/classes/OnboardingService.cls">
/**
 * Creates onboarding Cases and activates Accounts when Opportunities become Closed Won.
 * Bulk-safe: one SOQL query and at most two DML statements per transaction,
 * regardless of how many Opportunities are in the trigger batch.
 */
public with sharing class OnboardingService {
    @TestVisible
    private static final String CASE_ORIGIN = 'Sales Handoff';
    @TestVisible
    private static final String ACTIVE_STATUS = 'Active Customer';
    @TestVisible
    private static final Decimal HIGH_PRIORITY_AMOUNT = 100000;

    /**
     * @param newOpps Trigger.new
     * @param oldMap  Trigger.oldMap (null on insert)
     */
    public static void handleClosedWon(List<Opportunity> newOpps, Map<Id, Opportunity> oldMap) {
        Map<Id, Opportunity> wonByAccount = collectNewlyWon(newOpps, oldMap);
        if (wonByAccount.isEmpty()) {
            return;
        }

        List<Case> casesToInsert = new List<Case>();
        List<Account> accountsToUpdate = new List<Account>();
        for (Account acc : [
            SELECT Id, Name,
                (SELECT Id FROM Cases WHERE Is_Onboarding__c = true AND IsClosed = false LIMIT 1)
            FROM Account
            WHERE Id IN :wonByAccount.keySet()
            WITH USER_MODE
        ]) {
            accountsToUpdate.add(new Account(Id = acc.Id, Customer_Status__c = ACTIVE_STATUS));
            if (acc.Cases.isEmpty()) {
                casesToInsert.add(buildCase(acc, wonByAccount.get(acc.Id)));
            }
        }

        insert as user casesToInsert;
        update as user accountsToUpdate;
    }

    /** One entry per Account: the highest-value Opportunity that just became won. */
    private static Map<Id, Opportunity> collectNewlyWon(List<Opportunity> newOpps, Map<Id, Opportunity> oldMap) {
        Map<Id, Opportunity> wonByAccount = new Map<Id, Opportunity>();
        for (Opportunity opp : newOpps) {
            Opportunity old = oldMap == null ? null : oldMap.get(opp.Id);
            Boolean becameWon = opp.IsWon && (old == null || !old.IsWon);
            if (!becameWon || opp.AccountId == null) {
                continue;
            }
            Opportunity current = wonByAccount.get(opp.AccountId);
            if (current == null || amountOf(opp) > amountOf(current)) {
                wonByAccount.put(opp.AccountId, opp);
            }
        }
        return wonByAccount;
    }

    private static Case buildCase(Account acc, Opportunity opp) {
        return new Case(
            AccountId = acc.Id,
            Subject = 'Onboarding: ' + acc.Name,
            Origin = CASE_ORIGIN,
            Priority = amountOf(opp) >= HIGH_PRIORITY_AMOUNT ? 'High' : 'Medium',
            Is_Onboarding__c = true,
            Description = 'Created automatically from Closed Won opportunity ' + opp.Name
        );
    }

    private static Decimal amountOf(Opportunity opp) {
        return opp.Amount == null ? 0 : opp.Amount;
    }
}
</file>

<summary>Clean trigger-handler-service structure that follows the team standards and the design: logic-free trigger, one SOQL and two DML per transaction, user-mode data access and tests per acceptance criterion including bulk and run-as cases. Static analysis is clean after one fix iteration. No blocking issues; one medium configuration item and two low suggestions.</summary>
<finding severity="medium">"Sales Handoff" must exist as a value in the Case Origin picklist (StandardValueSet CaseOrigin), otherwise reports and list views will not show it as a proper value. Add it before deployment or include the StandardValueSet in the package.</finding>
<finding severity="low">Add a bypass switch (e.g. a custom permission checked in OpportunityTriggerHandler) so data migrations can load historical Closed Won deals without creating onboarding cases.</finding>
<finding severity="low">Consider moving the 100,000 threshold to custom metadata so Sales Ops can change it without a deployment.</finding>
<verdict>APPROVE</verdict>

<summary>Sharing is enforced on every class, all SOQL runs WITH USER_MODE and all DML runs as user, there is no dynamic SOQL and no hardcoded Ids, and access is granted through a narrow permission set rather than profiles. Two medium items concern permission-set scope and silent skips; nothing blocks release.</summary>
<finding severity="medium">The permission set gives reps edit access to Account.Customer_Status__c, so they can also change it by hand. If status must be system-controlled, make the field read-only for reps and perform only that update in a narrowly scoped system-mode helper.</finding>
<finding severity="medium">With user-mode queries, an Opportunity whose Account the rep cannot see is skipped silently. Log these cases (e.g. a platform event or an error log record) so onboarding is never missed without a trace.</finding>
<finding severity="low">The Case Description includes the Opportunity name; confirm deal names never contain information the onboarding team should not see.</finding>
<verdict>PASS</verdict>

<file path=".github/workflows/salesforce-ci.yml">
name: salesforce-ci

on:
  pull_request:
    paths: ["force-app/**", "config/**"]
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ["force-app/**", "config/**"]

env:
  TESTS: OnboardingServiceTest

jobs:
  static-analysis:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "21"
      - name: Install PMD
        run: |
          curl -sSL -o pmd.zip https://github.com/pmd/pmd/releases/download/pmd_releases%2F7.8.0/pmd-dist-7.8.0-bin.zip
          unzip -q pmd.zip
      - name: PMD Apex rules (same ruleset as the agent gate)
        run: pmd-bin-7.8.0/bin/pmd check -d force-app -R config/pmd-ruleset.xml -f text --no-progress

  validate:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    needs: static-analysis
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
